verdicts.name: Sirloin steak
issues: alias 'beef' should not land on lean-only top sirloin: someone typing 'beef' most likely means ground beef or a generic beef; routing it to a 188 kcal trimmed steak is arbitrary and hijacks the generic term. Keep 'beef' generic (no curated alias). 'steak', 'steaks' and 'beef steak' -> sirloin are sensible: sirloin is the most generic plain steak.

pair check: both halves top sirloin steak, separable lean only, choice; trim differs (cooked 0", raw 1/8") - acceptable per brief. Neither a 0" raw nor a 1/8" broiled top sirloin steak surfaced in 2 further searches (only 'top sirloin petite roast/filet' 0" raw 173408 and 'top sirloin filet' 0" grilled 174694, which are a different sub-cut).

verdicts.name: Filet mignon
issues: alias 'fillet' is a fish word for most people (salmon fillet, cod fillet); routing it to beef tenderloin is a wrong-food risk. Drop it. 'tenderloin' alone is ambiguous with pork tenderloin but beef is the more common unqualified meaning - kept.
pair itself is exact: tenderloin steak, lean only, 1/8" trim, choice, both halves.

summary: Checked all 29 red-meat/pork/lamb/processed entries on name, pair sameness, numbers, aliases and default; 55 USDA requests used. Every steak/roast pair is same cut and same 'separable lean only' on both halves (ribeye, NY strip, filet, flank, skirt, chuck, pork chop boneless top loin, pork ribs spareribs lean+fat, bacon cured raw vs cooked all check out); numbers are all plausible, including ground lamb and bison where raw is about equal to cooked because fat renders. Six FIXes: (1) Ground beef 85/15 raw exists - SR 171796 (the FDP-tagged generic), plus missing rawLabel; (2) Brisket raw can be the choice-grade 168657 to match the choice cooked half exactly; (3) Ham deli cooked 332397 and (4) Italian sausage cooked 746780 both 404 at USDA - replaced with FNDDS 2705878 'Ham' and 2706189 'Italian sausage' (identical P/C/F for the sausage); (5) Sirloin: drop alias 'beef' - a bare 'beef' should stay generic rather than land on trimmed sirloin, while 'steak'/'beef steak' -> sirloin is sensible; (6) Filet mignon: drop 'fillet' (a fish word). Sirloin trim mismatch (0" cooked / 1/8" raw) is acceptable and I could not find an exact-trim alternative either. Lamb chop's Australian pair is fine; a US domestic loin pair (172491 raw / 172492 broiled, 1/4" choice) does exist if a domestic entry is preferred. Eight adds: top round steak, eye of round roast (cooked-only - raw 746760 404s on direct fetch despite appearing in search), pork shoulder, Canadian bacon, pork belly, prosciutto, chorizo (cooked-only), bratwurst. Further candidates not added under the 8 cap: corned beef 170200, kielbasa 173877. Unsure: no plain 'ground beef'/'hamburger' alias exists on any entry, so the generic term relies on substring matching - worth deciding which lean % it should land on.
